main_edits.old_string: RoCE differs by merging the treatment and density-ratio components into a single exponential-tilting calibration model for each source-treatment pair, then using a variance- and discrepancy-aware aggregation rule to decide how much each source should contribute to the target estimand.
main_edits.new_string: RoCE differs by merging the treatment and density-ratio components into a single exponential-tilting calibration model for each source-treatment pair, then using a variance-minimizing aggregation rule with a Wald-type selection penalty---based on the standardized, rather than raw squared, discrepancy between each source-assisted and target-only estimator---to decide how much each source should contribute to the target estimand.

main_edits.old_string: \REQUIRE Target data $\mathcal{D}_t$, source data $\{\mathcal{D}_{s_j}\}_{j=1}^K$, feature map $\phi$, nuisance penalty grids, aggregation penalty grid, and $K_f$ two-level cross-fitting folds.
main_edits.new_string: \REQUIRE Target data $\mathcal{D}_t$, source data $\{\mathcal{D}_{s_j}\}_{j=1}^K$, feature map $\phi$, nuisance penalty grids, a fixed aggregation Wald threshold $1/\lambda$, and $K_f$ two-level cross-fitting folds.

main_edits.old_string: \STATE Keep $\mathcal{D}_{k_1}$ held out. Learn nuisance models, tune $\lambda$, and estimate aggregation weights only inside $\mathcal{T}_{k_1}=\mathcal{D}\setminus\mathcal{D}_{k_1}$.
main_edits.new_string: \STATE Keep $\mathcal{D}_{k_1}$ held out. Learn nuisance models (tuning the nuisance penalties) and estimate aggregation weights at the fixed aggregation Wald threshold $1/\lambda$, only inside $\mathcal{T}_{k_1}=\mathcal{D}\setminus\mathcal{D}_{k_1}$.

main_edits.old_string: All sites agree on the working feature map $\phi(\boldsymbol{X})$, the GLM response function $\psi$, the fold partition used for two-level cross-fitting, and candidate grids for the nuisance penalties $(\lambda_\gamma,\lambda_\alpha)$ and aggregation penalty $\lambda$.
main_edits.new_string: All sites agree on the working feature map $\phi(\boldsymbol{X})$, the GLM response function $\psi$, the fold partition used for two-level cross-fitting, candidate grids for the nuisance penalties $(\lambda_\gamma,\lambda_\alpha)$, and a fixed aggregation Wald threshold $1/\lambda$.

main_edits.old_string: Following the FACE validation strategy for adaptive aggregation \citep{han2025federated}, the aggregation penalty $\lambda$ is also selected inside $\mathcal{T}_{k_1}$, and the final weights $\widehat{\boldsymbol{\eta}}^{(-k_1)}$ are applied only to observations in the held-out outer fold.
main_edits.new_string: The aggregation penalty parameter $\lambda$ is not data-adaptively tuned: it is fixed at a Wald significance level (e.g.\ $1/\lambda=2$, i.e.\ $|\widehat{t}_j|>2$, $p<0.05$), the finite-sample analogue of the asymptotic threshold $1/\lambda\to\infty$ growing slower than $\sqrt{N_{\mathrm{all}}}$, exactly as the nuisance penalties use fixed grids in place of their asymptotic rates. The variance/discrepancy summaries entering the aggregation objective and the final weights $\widehat{\boldsymbol{\eta}}^{(-k_1)}$ are still computed only inside $\mathcal{T}_{k_1}$, and the weights are applied only to observations in the held-out outer fold.

main_edits.old_string: The framework involves two types of regularization parameters ($\lambda$) that must be tuned.
main_edits.new_string: The framework involves two types of regularization parameters. The nuisance penalties $(\lambda_\gamma,\lambda_\alpha)$ are selected by cross-validation, while the aggregation penalty $\lambda$ is fixed at a Wald significance threshold rather than tuned.

main_edits.old_string: The regularization parameter $\lambda$ in the aggregation objective~\cref{eq:final_opt} controls how aggressively RoCE borrows from source sites. Small $\lambda$ allows more borrowing and can reduce variance when source-assisted estimators are transportable, but it also increases exposure to negative transfer. Large $\lambda$ shrinks source weights toward zero, moving the estimator toward the target-only anchor and reducing transfer-bias risk at the cost of weaker precision gains.
main_edits.new_string: The parameter $\lambda$ in the aggregation objective~\cref{eq:final_opt} controls how aggressively RoCE borrows from source sites through the Wald inclusion threshold $1/\lambda$: source $s_j$ is admitted unpenalized when its standardized discrepancy satisfies $\widehat{t}_j\le 1/\lambda$, and shrunk toward zero when $\widehat{t}_j>1/\lambda$. A larger cutoff $1/\lambda$ (smaller $\lambda$) admits more sources and can reduce variance when source-assisted estimators are transportable, but it also increases exposure to negative transfer; a smaller cutoff (larger $\lambda$) excludes any source whose Wald statistic exceeds it, moving the estimator toward the target-only anchor and reducing transfer-bias risk at the cost of weaker precision gains. The asymptotic regime $\lambda\to 0$, $\lambda\sqrt{N_{\mathrm{all}}}\to\infty$ corresponds to a cutoff $1/\lambda$ that grows without bound but slower than $\sqrt{N_{\mathrm{all}}}$, so that informative sources ($\widehat{t}_j=O_p(1)$) are retained while biased sources ($\widehat{t}_j\to\infty$) are excluded.

main_edits.old_string:
A fixed grid $\Lambda$ (e.g.\ $[10^{-3}, 1]$) is not robust across problem scales because the useful range of $\lambda$ depends on the magnitudes of the variance components and the site discrepancies. To construct a data-adaptive grid, we identify the \emph{natural scale} $\lambda_{\mathrm{nat}}$ at which the penalty and variance terms are comparable.

For source site $s_j$, the unpenalized variance contribution is
\[
\sigma_j^2 \;\coloneqq\; \frac{\widehat{V}_{t,s_j}}{N_t} + \frac{\widehat{V}_{s_j}}{N_{s_j}},
\]
and the penalty scale is $d_j^2 \coloneqq (\widehat{\mu}^1_{ot} - \widehat{\mu}^1_{t,s_j})^2$.
Setting $\lambda \, d_j^2 = \sigma_j^2$ gives the transition point
$\lambda_j = \sigma_j^2 / d_j^2$.
When $d_j^2$ is very small (i.e.\ the source and target estimates nearly agree, suggesting low bias), we floor $d_j^2$ at $\sigma_j^2$ to avoid $\lambda_j \to \infty$:
\[
\lambda_j \;=\; \frac{\sigma_j^2}{\max(d_j^2,\; \sigma_j^2)}.
\]
The natural scale is defined as
\begin{equation*}
\lambda_{\mathrm{nat}} \;=\; \operatorname{median}_{j=1,\ldots,K}\; \lambda_j,
\end{equation*}
and the search grid spans two orders of magnitude on each side:
\[
\Lambda \;=\; \bigl\{\lambda : \lambda \in [10^{-2}\,\lambda_{\mathrm{nat}},\; 10^{2}\,\lambda_{\mathrm{nat}}]\bigr\},
\]
with $|\Lambda|$ evenly spaced on the log scale (e.g.\ 100 points).
The grid is recomputed inside each outer training set and spans the transition from weakly regularized weights to strong shrinkage toward the target-only estimator.

We select $\lambda$ by the sample-splitting validation idea used in FACE \citep{han2025federated}. For an outer evaluation fold $k_1$, let $\mathcal{T}_{k_1}=\mathcal{D}\setminus\mathcal{D}_{k_1}$ be the data available for nuisance fitting and weight tuning. Split $\mathcal{T}_{k_1}$ into $M$ inner folds. For inner fold $m$, let $\mathcal{T}_{k_1,-m}$ be the inner-training data and $\mathcal{I}_m$ the inner-validation data, keeping site proportions approximately fixed.

For each candidate $\lambda\in\Lambda$, all nuisance parameters and variance/discrepancy summaries are computed on the inner-training data $\mathcal{T}_{k_1,-m}$, and the target solves the penalized aggregation problem:
\[
\widehat{\boldsymbol{\eta}}^{(-k_1,-m)}(\lambda)
=
\arg\min_{\boldsymbol{\eta}}
\left\{
\widehat{\Var}_{\mathrm{tr},m}(\boldsymbol{\eta})
+\lambda\sum_{j=1}^K|\eta_j|
\left(\widehat{\mu}^{1,\mathrm{tr}}_{ot,m}-\widehat{\mu}^{1,\mathrm{tr}}_{t,s_j,m}\right)^2
\right\}.
\]
In parallel, each site computes validation summaries on $\mathcal{I}_m$ using nuisance parameters trained on $\mathcal{T}_{k_1,-m}$; no individual-level validation records are shared. The candidate $\lambda$ is evaluated by plugging the training-set weights into the validation-set penalized criterion:
\begin{equation}\label{eq:lambda_validation_loss}
Q_{\mathrm{val},m}(\lambda)
=
N_{\mathrm{val},m}\,
\widehat{\Var}_{\mathrm{val},m}\!\left\{\widehat{\boldsymbol{\eta}}^{(-k_1,-m)}(\lambda)\right\}
+\lambda\sum_{j=1}^K
\left|\widehat{\eta}^{(-k_1,-m)}_j(\lambda)\right|
\left(\widehat{\mu}^{1,\mathrm{val}}_{ot,m}-\widehat{\mu}^{1,\mathrm{val}}_{t,s_j,m}\right)^2,
\end{equation}
where $N_{\mathrm{val},m}$ is the total validation sample size across sites in $\mathcal{I}_m$ and $\widehat{\Var}_{\mathrm{val},m}\{\eta\}$ is the RoCE variance expression in \cref{eq:final_opt} evaluated with validation-fold variance/covariance summaries and the fixed weights $\eta$.
The selected aggregation tuning parameter is
\begin{equation*}
\widehat{\lambda}^{(-k_1)}
=
\arg\min_{\lambda\in\Lambda}
\frac{1}{M}\sum_{m=1}^M Q_{\mathrm{val},m}(\lambda).
\end{equation*}
As in FACE, the split can be repeated over several inner folds (e.g., five-fold validation), and the selected value minimizes the average validation criterion. As a conservative finite-sample variant, one may choose the largest $\lambda$ whose average validation criterion is within one estimated standard error, or within a small relative tolerance, of the minimum. After $\widehat{\lambda}^{(-k_1)}$ is selected, the aggregation weights $\widehat{\boldsymbol{\eta}}^{(-k_1)}$ are recomputed on all of $\mathcal{T}_{k_1}$ and then applied only to the outer evaluation fold $\mathcal{D}_{k_1}$.
main_edits.new_string:
Because the aggregation penalty acts through the self-normalized Wald statistic $\widehat{t}_j$ in \cref{eq:final_opt}, $\lambda$ is scale-free and does not require a problem-scale-dependent grid: there is no variance-versus-discrepancy balancing and no flooring of the discrepancy. Accordingly, $\lambda$ is not selected by data-adaptive cross-validation. Instead it is fixed at a single Wald significance level, with the inclusion threshold $1/\lambda$ set to a constant (e.g.\ $1/\lambda=2$, i.e.\ admit source $s_j$ iff $\widehat{t}_j\le 2$, corresponding to $p<0.05$). This fixed threshold is the finite-sample analogue of the asymptotic rate $1/\lambda\to\infty$ growing slower than $\sqrt{N_{\mathrm{all}}}$, mirroring the way the nuisance penalties use fixed grids in place of their asymptotic rates.

For an outer evaluation fold $k_1$, let $\mathcal{T}_{k_1}=\mathcal{D}\setminus\mathcal{D}_{k_1}$ be the data available for nuisance fitting and weight estimation. All variance, covariance, and discrepancy summaries entering \cref{eq:final_opt}, and hence the standardized statistics $\widehat{t}_j$, are computed on $\mathcal{T}_{k_1}$; the aggregation weights $\widehat{\boldsymbol{\eta}}^{(-k_1)}$ are obtained by solving \cref{eq:final_opt} at the fixed threshold $1/\lambda$ and are then applied only to the outer evaluation fold $\mathcal{D}_{k_1}$. No inner-fold validation of $\lambda$ is performed. The optional FACE-style validation criterion $Q_{\mathrm{val},m}(\lambda)$ that would be used if one instead tuned $\lambda$ over a grid is recorded in \cref{eq:lambda_validation_loss_app} for completeness.

main_edits.old_string: The aggregation theory assumes that the population quadratic variance is locally strictly convex on the oracle subspace, that non-informative sources are separated from the target by a beta-min condition, and that the aggregation penalty satisfies $\lambda\to\infty$ while $\lambda/\sqrt{N_{\mathrm{all}}}\to0$. Under fixed separation, the penalty dominates the discrepancy term for biased sources and sets their weights to zero with probability tending to one; for informative sources, the penalty is asymptotically negligible at the $N_{\mathrm{all}}^{-1/2}$ scale.
main_edits.new_string: The aggregation theory assumes that the population quadratic variance is locally strictly convex on the oracle subspace, that non-informative sources are separated from the target by a beta-min condition (fixed separation $b_0>0$, so that $b_0\sqrt{N_{\mathrm{all}}}\to\infty$), and that the aggregation penalty satisfies $\lambda\to 0$ while $\lambda\sqrt{N_{\mathrm{all}}}\to\infty$ (equivalently the Wald inclusion threshold $1/\lambda\to\infty$ but slower than $\sqrt{N_{\mathrm{all}}}$). The truncated-Wald penalty $(\lambda\,\widehat{t}_j-1)_+$ uses self-normalized statistics: for a biased source, $\widehat{t}_j=\Theta_p(\sqrt{N_{\mathrm{all}}}\,b_j)\to\infty$, so the active penalty $\sim\lambda\sqrt{N_{\mathrm{all}}}\,b_j$ dominates the $O(N_{\mathrm{all}}^{-1})$ variance gradient at $\eta_j=0$ and sets the weight to zero with probability tending to one; for an informative source, $\widehat{t}_j=O_p(1)\le 1/\lambda$ with probability tending to one, so the source is kept unpenalized at its variance-minimizing coordinate.

main_edits.old_string: \item Evaluate $Q_{\mathrm{val},k_2}(\lambda)$ by plugging $\widehat{\boldsymbol{\eta}}^{(-k_1,-k_2)}(\lambda)$ into the validation penalized criterion in \cref{eq:lambda_validation_loss}.

supp_edits.new_string:
The penalized objective from \maincref{eq:final_opt} uses the truncated-Wald penalty, the finite-sample remedy of FACE \citep{han2025federated} (Remark 9). Recall $\widehat{L}(\eta)=N_{\mathrm{all}}\cdot\widehat{\Var}(\widehat{\mu}^1_{\mathrm{agg}}(\eta))$ is the rescaled (asymptotic) variance, so its gradient and Hessian are $\Theta(1)$:
\begin{equation}\label{eq:penalized_obj}
\widehat{\eta} = \arg\min_\eta \left\{ \widehat{L}(\eta) + \sum_{j=1}^K \bigl(\lambda\,\widehat{t}_j - 1\bigr)_+ |\eta_j| \right\},
\qquad
\widehat{t}_j \coloneqq \frac{\bigl|\widehat{\mu}^1_{ot} - \widehat{\mu}^1_{t,s_j}\bigr|}{\widehat{\mathrm{SE}}(\mathrm{disc}_j)},
\end{equation}
where $\widehat{t}_j$ is the self-normalized Wald statistic of the discrepancy $\mathrm{disc}_j \coloneqq \widehat{\mu}^1_{ot} - \widehat{\mu}^1_{t,s_j}$, with estimated standard error
\[
\widehat{\mathrm{SE}}(\mathrm{disc}_j)^2
=
\frac{\widehat{V}_{ot}}{N_t} + \frac{\widehat{V}_{t,s_j}}{N_t} + \frac{\widehat{V}_{s_j}}{N_{s_j}} - \frac{2\,\widehat{C}_{ot,s_j}}{N_t}
=
\widehat{\Var}\bigl(\widehat{\mu}^1_{t,s_j} - \widehat{\mu}^1_{ot}\bigr).
\]
(The implementation in \texttt{weight\_optimization.cpp} equivalently minimizes the \emph{unscaled} variance $\widehat{V}(\eta)=\widehat{L}(\eta)/N_{\mathrm{all}}$ with the same penalty rescaled by $N_{\mathrm{all}}$; the two formulations have identical minimizers and selection sets, see \cref{rem:soft_threshold}.)
Here $\lambda > 0$ is an \emph{inclusion threshold}: the $L_1$ coefficient $(\lambda\widehat{t}_j - 1)_+$ vanishes (site kept, unpenalized efficient coordinate) when $\widehat{t}_j \le 1/\lambda$ and is positive otherwise. In contrast to a penalty driven to infinity with $N_{\mathrm{all}}$, the relevant asymptotic regime is $1/\lambda \to \infty$ but $\lambda\sqrt{N_{\mathrm{all}}} \to \infty$ (i.e.\ $\lambda \to 0$); see \cref{asmp:aggregation}(b)--(c).

The penalty coefficient $(\lambda\widehat{t}_j - 1)_+$ is driven by the standardized Wald statistic $\widehat{t}_j$ of the discrepancy $\mathrm{disc}_j$, not by its raw square. A \emph{biased} site (separation $b_j \coloneqq |\text{plim}(\widehat{\mu}^1_{t,s_j}) - \mu^1| > 0$) has $\widehat{\mathrm{SE}}(\mathrm{disc}_j) = \Theta_p(N_{\mathrm{all}}^{-1/2})$ while $\mathrm{disc}_j \xrightarrow{p} b_j$, so $\widehat{t}_j = \Theta_p(\sqrt{N_{\mathrm{all}}}\, b_j) \to \infty$, the penalty diverges, and $\widehat{\eta}_j \to 0$. An \emph{informative} site has $\mathrm{disc}_j = O_p(N_{\mathrm{all}}^{-1/2})$ and the same $\Theta(N_{\mathrm{all}}^{-1/2})$ standard error, so $\widehat{t}_j = O_p(1)$ is asymptotically bounded; once the inclusion threshold $1/\lambda$ exceeds this $O_p(1)$ statistic the site is kept with zero penalty (efficient OLS coordinate). The standard error $\widehat{\mathrm{SE}}(\mathrm{disc}_j)$ is a plug-in built from the consistently estimated variance/covariance components of \cref{lem:var_components_agg}, hence $\sqrt{N_{\mathrm{all}}}$-consistent for the true discrepancy standard error, so $\widehat{t}_j$ is a well-defined studentized statistic.

supp_edits.old_string: For the asymptotic arguments below, $\lambda$ may be deterministic or data-adaptive, provided it is measurable with respect to the outer training data and satisfies \cref{asmp:aggregation}(b)--(c) with probability tending to one. The inner validation construction preserves the cross-fitting independence needed for the influence-function expansion because the training summaries used to compute $\widehat{\eta}^{(-k,-m)}(\lambda)$, the validation summaries used to choose $\widehat{\lambda}^{(-k)}$, and the final outer evaluation fold $\mathcal{D}_k$ are separated. Consequently neither $\widehat{\lambda}^{(-k)}$ nor $\widehat{\eta}^{(-k)}$ uses the outer evaluation fold $\mathcal{D}_k$.
supp_edits.new_string:
For the asymptotic arguments below, $\lambda$ is the Wald-significance inclusion threshold of \cref{eq:penalized_obj}: it may be deterministic or data-adaptive, provided it is measurable with respect to the outer training data and satisfies \cref{asmp:aggregation}(b)--(c) (i.e.\ $\lambda \to 0$ and $\lambda\sqrt{N_{\mathrm{all}}} \to \infty$, equivalently $1/\lambda \to \infty$ slower than $\sqrt{N_{\mathrm{all}}}$) with probability tending to one; it is \emph{not} a parameter driven to infinity. The inner validation construction preserves the cross-fitting independence needed for the influence-function expansion because the training summaries used to compute $\widehat{\eta}^{(-k,-m)}(\lambda)$, the validation summaries used to choose $\widehat{\lambda}^{(-k)}$, and the final outer evaluation fold $\mathcal{D}_k$ are separated. Consequently neither $\widehat{\lambda}^{(-k)}$ nor $\widehat{\eta}^{(-k)}$ uses the outer evaluation fold $\mathcal{D}_k$.
In the implementation, $\lambda$ is fixed at a Wald significance level rather than literally driven to zero: the constant $\texttt{AGG\_WALD\_LAMBDA}=0.5$ sets $1/\lambda = 2$ (so a site is penalized when $|\widehat{t}_j| > 2$, i.e.\ at the $p < 0.05$ level), and the data-adaptive path $\texttt{.aggregation\_lambda\_grid}$ returns this single significance-level point rather than a data-adaptive ``natural scale'' grid. This is the finite-sample analogue of the asymptotic threshold, exactly as the nuisance and aggregation penalties use fixed grids in place of their asymptotic rates.

supp_edits.old_string:
The penalty in \cref{eq:penalized_obj} is an adaptive $\ell_1$ penalty, so its selection mechanism is the same as soft-thresholding in penalized quadratic optimization. To see this, consider the special case in which $\widehat{H}$ is diagonal, say $\widehat{H}=\mathrm{diag}(\widehat{h}_1,\ldots,\widehat{h}_K)$ with $\widehat{h}_j>0$. Then the objective separates coordinatewise, and each $\widehat{\eta}_j$ minimizes
\[
\widehat{h}_j \eta_j^2 + \widehat{g}_j \eta_j + \lambda \widehat{d}_j |\eta_j|,
\qquad
\widehat{d}_j \coloneqq (\widehat{\mu}^1_{ot} - \widehat{\mu}^1_{t,s_j})^2.
\]
Completing the square yields the explicit solution
\[
\widehat{\eta}_j
=
-\frac{1}{2\widehat{h}_j}\,
\mathrm{sign}(\widehat{g}_j)\,
\Bigl(|\widehat{g}_j|-\lambda \widehat{d}_j\Bigr)_+,
\]
which is the usual soft-thresholding rule: if $|\widehat{g}_j|\le \lambda \widehat{d}_j$, then $\widehat{\eta}_j=0$; otherwise the unconstrained quadratic solution is shrunk toward zero by the amount $\lambda \widehat{d}_j/(2\widehat{h}_j)$. In the general non-diagonal case, the coordinates are coupled through $\widehat{H}$, so one no longer has a closed-form coordinatewise solution, but the same $\ell_1$-induced shrinkage-and-selection interpretation remains valid.
supp_edits.new_string:
The penalty in \cref{eq:penalized_obj} is an adaptive $\ell_1$ penalty, so its selection mechanism is the same as soft-thresholding in penalized quadratic optimization; this is FACE \citep{han2025federated} Remark 9's finite-sample remedy. We display the rule for the \emph{unscaled} per-observation variance objective $\widehat{V}(\eta)=\widehat{L}(\eta)/N_{\mathrm{all}}$ actually minimized in \texttt{weight\_optimization.cpp}, so the coordinate coefficients carry the $1/N$ factors of that implementation; the rescaled objective $\widehat{L}$ used elsewhere gives the same selection set. Consider the special case in which the unscaled Hessian is diagonal, with diagonal entries $\widehat{H}_{jj}=\partial^2\widehat{V}/\partial\eta_j^2>0$. Then the objective separates coordinatewise, and each $\widehat{\eta}_j$ minimizes
\[
\tfrac{1}{2}\widehat{H}_{jj}\, \eta_j^2 + \widehat{b}_j\, \eta_j + \bigl(\lambda\widehat{t}_j - 1\bigr)_+ |\eta_j|,
\qquad
\widehat{b}_j \coloneqq \frac{\partial \widehat{V}}{\partial \eta_j}\Big|_{\eta=0} = \frac{2\bigl(\widehat{C}_{ot,s_j} - \widehat{V}_{ot}\bigr)}{N_t},
\]
where $\widehat{b}_j = O_p(N_{\mathrm{all}}^{-1})$ is the variance gradient at $\eta=0$. Completing the square yields the explicit solution
\[
\widehat{\eta}_j
=
\mathrm{SoftThreshold}\!\left(\eta_j^{\mathrm{OLS}},\;\frac{(\lambda\widehat{t}_j - 1)_+}{\widehat{H}_{jj}}\right),
\qquad
\eta_j^{\mathrm{OLS}} \coloneqq -\frac{\widehat{b}_j}{\widehat{H}_{jj}} = \frac{2\bigl(\widehat{V}_{ot} - \widehat{C}_{ot,s_j}\bigr)}{N_t\,\widehat{H}_{jj}},
\]
where $\eta_j^{\mathrm{OLS}}$ is the unpenalized variance-minimizing coordinate (matching the closed-form code path in \texttt{weight\_optimization.cpp}). Equivalently, the KKT selection rule is
\[
\widehat{\eta}_j = 0
\quad\Longleftrightarrow\quad
|\widehat{b}_j| \le \bigl(\lambda\widehat{t}_j - 1\bigr)_+,
\]
so a site is dropped exactly when its truncated-Wald threshold exceeds the magnitude of the variance gradient $\widehat{b}_j = O_p(N_{\mathrm{all}}^{-1})$. In the general non-diagonal case, the coordinates are coupled through the Hessian, so one no longer has a closed-form coordinatewise solution, but the same $\ell_1$-induced shrinkage-and-selection interpretation remains valid.

supp_edits.new_string:
Assume the standardized separation diverges, $b_{0,N}\,\sqrt{N_{\mathrm{all}}}\to\infty$, so the biased Wald statistics $\widehat{t}_j = \Theta_p(\sqrt{N_{\mathrm{all}}}\,b_{j,N})\to\infty$. A special case is \emph{fixed separation}: $b_{0,N}\ge b_0>0$, which implies this automatically. (The $\sqrt{N_{\mathrm{all}}}$ scaling now sits inside the self-normalized Wald statistic, so the penalty no longer multiplies $b^2$.)
(c) (Threshold rate) The inclusion threshold satisfies $\lambda \to 0$ and $\lambda\,\sqrt{N_{\mathrm{all}}} \to \infty$; equivalently $1/\lambda \to \infty$ but slower than $\sqrt{N_{\mathrm{all}}}$. Under this rate, $P(\widehat{t}_j > 1/\lambda)\to 0$ for informative sites (kept unpenalized) while $\widehat{t}_j > 1/\lambda$ w.p.a.1 for biased sites (excluded).

supp_edits.old_string: When $\lambda$ is selected by the validation rule in the main manuscript, \cref{asmp:aggregation}(b)--(c) should be read as high-probability conditions on the selected sequence $\widehat{\lambda}$. Equivalently, the theorem below is conditional on the event that the validation-selected penalty lies in the oracle-selection window. This separates the finite-sample tuning rule from the asymptotic support-recovery requirement.
supp_edits.new_string: When $\lambda$ is selected by the validation rule in the main manuscript, \cref{asmp:aggregation}(b) (separation $b_{0,N}\sqrt{N_{\mathrm{all}}}\to\infty$) and \cref{asmp:aggregation}(c) (threshold rate $\lambda\to 0$, $\lambda\sqrt{N_{\mathrm{all}}}\to\infty$) should be read as high-probability conditions on the selected sequence $\widehat{\lambda}$. Equivalently, the theorem below is conditional on the event that the validation-selected threshold lies in the oracle-selection window: $1/\widehat{\lambda}$ sits above the $O_p(1)$ informative Wald statistics but below the diverging biased ones. This separates the finite-sample tuning rule from the asymptotic support-recovery requirement; in practice $\lambda$ is fixed at a significance level ($1/\lambda = 2$) rather than literally driven to zero, the finite-sample analogue of the asymptotic threshold.

$
hence $(\widehat{\mu}^1_{ot}-\widehat{\mu}^1_{t,s_j})^2=O_p(N_{\mathrm{all}}^{-1})$ and therefore the penalty contribution on $\mathbb{R}_{\mathcal{S}^*}$ is

supp_edits.new_string:
\widetilde{\eta} \;=\; \arg\min_{\eta\in\mathbb{R}_{\mathcal{S}^*}}
\left\{ \widehat{L}(\eta) + \sum_{j=1}^K \bigl(\lambda\widehat{t}_j - 1\bigr)_+ |\eta_j| \right\}.
\]
On $\mathbb{R}_{\mathcal{S}^*}$, only coordinates $j\in\mathcal{S}^*$ can be nonzero, so the penalty term reduces to $\sum_{j\in\mathcal{S}^*}(\lambda\widehat{t}_j - 1)_+ |\eta_j|$.
By \cref{thm:main} and the site-ratio regularity, for each fixed informative $j\in\mathcal{S}^*$, $\mathrm{disc}_j=\widehat{\mu}^1_{ot}-\widehat{\mu}^1_{t,s_j}=O_p(N_{\mathrm{all}}^{-1/2})$, while $\widehat{\mathrm{SE}}(\mathrm{disc}_j)=\Theta_p(N_{\mathrm{all}}^{-1/2})$ by \cref{lem:var_components_agg}, so the Wald statistic $\widehat{t}_j=|\mathrm{disc}_j|/\widehat{\mathrm{SE}}(\mathrm{disc}_j)=O_p(1)$.
Under the threshold rate $1/\lambda\to\infty$ of \cref{asmp:aggregation}(c), $P(\widehat{t}_j > 1/\lambda)\to 0$, hence $(\lambda\widehat{t}_j - 1)_+ = 0$ w.p.a.1 for every $j\in\mathcal{S}^*$.
